species.name: ProD, product converted from the PreC pool

interactions.note: Inducer-driven KinA activation, shared by all three candidates. The inactive form is not a state: total KinA is calibrated and flat per the description, so the inactive pool is (Atot - Aa). Dose enters as the condition-owned constant u.
KinA deactivation (dephosphorylation, not proteolysis), written as removal because the inactive form is not a state. Shared by all candidates.

KinA-catalysed RegB activation, saturating at Btot, with BX-11 as a fixed 95% multiplicative block. This is one of the two contested edges: ProD appears as a modifier only in candidate M3_ff_feedback, where the rate carries an extra 1/(1 + D/K_fb) factor. In M1 and M2 the D participant is absent.
RegB deactivation, first order. Shared by all candidates.

PreC to ProD conversion catalysed by active RegB. PreC is not a state; the precursor is (Ctot - D) by conservation of the ~5 uM pool. Shared by all candidates — the module was designed around this edge and nothing in the description casts doubt on its existence, only on its exclusivity.
First-order loss of ProD, lumping turnover and dilution as the description does. Shared by all candidates.

The second contested edge: a RegB-independent conversion of PreC catalysed directly by KinA_p, present in M2_feedforward and M3_ff_feedback and absent in M1_chain. Listed here because the network is the union over the candidate set; which candidates carry it is stated per candidate.

parameters.source: no literature value exists for a synthetic module with no host homologues; order-of-magnitude placeholder consistent with an activation resolved over tens of minutes
no measured phosphatase activity; placeholder on the same timescale as the activation step
placeholder; the description says RegB activation requires KinA but gives no rate
placeholder chosen so that a few uM of ProD accumulate over the 120 min window from a 5 uM precursor pool
description says ProD is lost slowly by turnover and dilution; placeholder half-life of about an hour

decisions.decision: The candidate set is a three-rung ladder — M1_chain, then M2_feedforward = M1 + one parameter, then M3_ff_feedback = M2 + one parameter — rather than three unrelated wirings.
alternatives_considered: a fourth candidate with feedback but no direct route, to break the nesting
three structurally independent mechanisms (e.g. a basal conversion source, cooperative RegB activation, precursor-limited saturation)
decisions.question: Nesting is what makes the AIC comparison interpretable: each step costs exactly one parameter, so a large weight on M3 means both additions earned their keep and a weight on M2 means only the first did. The cost is that a feedback-without-route mechanism is not represented, so if ProD turns out not to rise under BX-11 the ladder cannot separate 'feedback only' from 'neither' in one pass.

decisions.decision: The hypothesis space is taken directly from the two open questions the description states, and from nothing else.
alternatives_considered: enumerate every kinetic variant that the data could in principle distinguish
restrict to the designed wiring and treat the open questions as noise

decisions.decision: Feedback is placed on RegB activation rather than on KinA activation or on the conversion step itself.
alternatives_considered: ProD inhibits its own conversion beyond the (Ctot - D) depletion already present
decisions.question: Is RegB activation the right site for the anecdotal product feedback? The description places it 'somewhere in the module' with no assay. Feedback onto J1 would show up as a non-monotone KinA_p, and feedback onto the conversion step is nearly degenerate with the precursor depletion term already present, so the RegB site is the one with a clean signature — but if the data show a KinA_p droop instead, this candidate is testing the wrong site and the ladder should be rebuilt.

decisions.decision: Everything not under test is held identical across the three candidates: same states, same conserved pools, same BX-11 encoding, same fixed totals, same bounds on the shared parameters.
alternatives_considered: let each candidate carry its own best-suited parameterisation and bounds
decisions.question: An information-criterion comparison is only about the structural difference if nothing else varies. Divergent bounds or observable choices between candidates would put a fitting artefact into the AIC difference and there would be no way to tell it apart from mechanism.

decisions.decision: BX-11 is a fixed 95% block on RegB activation in every candidate, not an estimated efficacy.
alternatives_considered: estimate the residual activity fraction, shared across candidates
decisions.question: A free residual-activity parameter is the most dangerous confound in this comparison: it is the one knob that lets M1_chain mimic a direct conversion route by leaking RegB activity under the inhibitor. Holding it fixed at the description's in vitro figure is what keeps the discrimination about mechanism. If the winning candidate misfits the BX-11 conditions in a way that a larger leak would fix, this is the assumption to revisit first — and revisiting it means refitting all three, not just the winner.

decisions.decision: The top-level antimony and parameters duplicate M1_chain.
alternatives_considered: duplicate the most complex candidate instead
decisions.question: Backward compatibility only, per the contract: the top-level fields are what a single-model consumer of this artifact would read. M1 is used because privileging the null costs nothing if a consumer ignores the candidate set, while privileging the richest candidate would silently pick a winner.

species.denotes: active (phosphorylated) KinA — the measured KinA_p peptide; the inactive pool is implicit as Atot - Aa
species.unit_convention: fraction of total KinA; total normalised to 1 (the lab note reports active forms against a total normalised to 1)
species.lump_membership: Aa is the single active form; no multi-site states are distinguished

species.denotes: active (phosphorylated) RegB — the measured RegB_p peptide; inactive pool implicit as Btot - Ba
species.unit_convention: fraction of total RegB; total normalised to 1
species.lump_membership: Ba is the single active form; deactivation lumped into one first-order step (J4)

species.denotes: the product ProD, measured directly as ProD_uM; the precursor PreC is implicit as Ctot - D
species.lump_membership: D is ProD alone; PreC is not a state but the conserved remainder of the 5 uM pool

parameters.role: inducer dose, set per condition by the condition table
parameters.convention: relative units against the standard stock (0.25, 1, 4)

parameters.role: BX-11 inhibitor switch, set per condition (0 untreated, 1 treated); scales RegB activation by (1 - 0.95*bx11)
parameters.convention: 0/1 flag; >90% inhibition per the lab note
